question: For perester synthesis from benzyl cyanide and TBHP, how should temperature, catalyst and time be chosen from the literature and reaction-competition evidence?

scientific_facts.text: The literature record (DOI: 10.1039/C6RA27921J) reports benzyl cyanide 1 mmol, TBHP 4 equivalents and Cu(OAc)2 10 mol%, without added solvent, in air at room temperature for 5 h. TBHP was supplied as a 70 wt% aqueous solution, so absence of added solvent does not mean anhydrous conditions.

Reported isolated perester yield is 80% at room temperature, 40% at 50 °C and 5% at 80 °C. At 80 °C, benzoic acid is the main product (85% isolated yield). For a perester target, start near the literature temperature rather than importing the project's higher temperatures.

Propose 20/25/30 °C checks starting at 25 °C, with samples at 1/3/5 h and analysis of perester and benzoic acid. The 5-h endpoint is the literature baseline; additional sampling is proposed. Initially retain the reported Cu(OAc)2 and TBHP proportions.

Route 4 contributes a decision sequence, not transferable parameters: its current apparent Ea is 4.495 kJ/mol and main total order is 10.419. Routes 2 and 3 show why reaction competition should be checked over time. Measure time profiles and selectivity before choosing heating, feed adjustment or shorter residence in the new chemistry.

These are literature baselines combined with conditional planning rules. New-system kinetics, thermal properties and side-reaction networks remain uncalibrated; no borrowed-parameter yield or validated tube dimension is claimed.

literature.authors: H. Hashemi; D. Saberi; S. Poorsadeghi; Kh. Niknam
facts: Benzyl cyanide 1 mmol, TBHP 4 mmol, Cu(OAc)2 10 mol%, no added solvent, air, room temperature, 5 h; TBHP supplied as 70 wt% aqueous solution.
Model-substrate isolated perester yields: room temperature 80%, 50 °C 40%, 80 °C 5%; at 80 °C benzoic acid is the principal product, 85%.
These are external observations, not Path4 predictions. Aliphatic cyanides and 4-nitrobenzyl cyanide are not supported by the demonstrated perester scope.
